text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
ZYCIE
- Police removed Solidarity trade unionists from the treasury ministry in Warsaw yesterday. Solidarity activists and opposition parliamentarians alleged violent treatment by police.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) and the the socialist Union of Labour (UP) have agreed to advance legislation aimed at continuation of Poland's reforms and regulations on a political ethical code.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- WZI Deblin military engineering plant in cooperation with Denmark's Silicon and Barthold firms have offered power generators to the Polish Army. The products' technological standards meet NATO requirements.

- The Huta Ostrowiec steelmill's general shareholders meeting scheduled for April 9 will propose increasing share capital by 61 percent through an issue of 6 million new shares and offer them to its creditors, the company said.

- The Poznan-based Bank Staropolski (BS) has called a general shareholders' meeting for April 7 to decide on a new share issue worth 10 million zlotys to be offered to present shareholders and changes in the board of the bank, BS spokesperson Zbigniew Przybylczak said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Over 100 travel agencies will take part in the Summer '97 tourist and leisure fair in Warsaw on April 18-20.
- Germany's Pneumant tyre company, controlled by SP Reifenwerke, is planning to sell 50,000 tyres for passenger cars in Poland this year, Pneumant Reifen GMBH director Rainer Schieben said.
- Poland issued 12,000 work permits to foreigners last year, 1,500 more than in 1995, the interior ministry said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The court appointed management of Fenix insurance firm has filed for bankruptcy. The firm's customers will receive damages due, its court-appointed manager Ewa Orzechowska said.
- The listed Mostostal Export will build an office block in Warsaw contracted by the Arcon company and worth 4.8 million zlotys.
ZYCIE

- Agora, publisher of Gazeta Wyborcza daily, will buy a 20 percent stake in Canal Plus Polska television from Polcom Invest, which holds a 67 percent stake in the company, and the Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy will buy an 11 percent stake in the broadcaster, the companies said.

- Israel's Elbit company said Boeing had no right to integrate Israeli NT-D missiles contracted by the Polish Army with other systems of Poland's Huzar military helicopter as this would mean passing technology to a competitor, Elbit's president Emmanuel Gill said.
PARKIET

- The listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych and its Bank Gdanski subsidiary have hired the U.S.'s McKinsey consulting firm to produce the banks' operational strategy, BIG's spokesperson Wojciech Kaczorowski said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
